Parses SUSE OVAL XML data and converts it into structured vulnerability definition models, handling multiple SUSE/openSUSE distribution variants and their version formats.

## Key Components

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `ConvertToModel` | Entry point that converts a parsed OVAL `Root` into a map of OS version → `[]models.Definition` |
| `parseTests` | Resolves OVAL test references into `rpmInfoTest` structs (name, version, arch, signing key) |
| `parseDefinitions` | Iterates OVAL definitions, extracts CVEs, bugzillas, CPEs, references, and groups packages by OS version |
| `collectSUSEPacks` | Routes criteria walking based on XML filename (special-cases openSUSE 12.x) |
| `walkCriteria` / `walkCriterion` | Recursively traverses OVAL `Criteria`/`Criterions` trees to extract OS versions and affected packages |
| `isOSComment` | Identifies whether a criterion comment refers to an OS version vs. a package |
| `getOSVersion` | Normalizes platform name strings (e.g. `sles15-sp2`, `openSUSE Leap 15.4`) into a canonical `"major.minor"` version string |
| `distroPackage` | Internal struct pairing an OS version string with a `models.Package` |

## Usage Example

```go
import (
    "encoding/xml"
    "os"

    "github.com/vulsio/goval-dictionary/fetcher/suse"
)

data, _ := os.ReadFile("suse.linux.enterprise.server.15.xml")

var root suse.Root
xml.Unmarshal(data, &root)

// Returns map[osVersion][]models.Definition
defs, err := suse.ConvertToModel("suse.linux.enterprise.server.15.xml", &root)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

for osVer, definitions := range defs {
    fmt.Printf("OS: %s — %d definitions\n", osVer, len(definitions))
}
```

## Notes

- XML filenames drive parsing behavior: legacy OVAL files (`opensuse.1*`, `sles.9/10`) extract CVEs from the definition title rather than the advisory block.
- When the `no-details` Viper flag is set, advisory metadata (severity, CPEs, bugzillas, references) is stripped before storage to reduce DB size.
- `getOSVersion` handles `suse*`, `sled*`, `sles*`, `core9`, `openSUSE`, and `SUSE Linux Enterprise` prefixes with service-pack suffix normalization (e.g. `sp2` → `.2`).
